jobs.occupation: Business Development Senior Officer (d/f/m) (ECHO) (Business-Development-Manager/in)
jobs.description: IRC (International Rescue Committee) Germany is seeking aBusiness Development Senior Officer (d/f/m) (ECHO)- in Berlin / Bonn or Remote (within Germany) | ASAP |- full-time (40 hours/week) | Initially for 2 yearsAbout Us Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. In 2016, IRC Germany was founded and engages in global humanitarian work as well as throughout Germany in the areas of education, economic wellbeing, and safety, legal protection, and empowerment.The Crisis Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) Department runs the IRC’s humanitarian, recovery, and development programs in five regions: West & Central Africa, East Africa, Middle East and North Africa, Asia, and Latin America. Within CRRD, the Award Management Unit (AMU)’s Grants Operations & Analytics Team (GOAT) supports pre- and post-award work for projects managed by Technical Excellence, Global Supply Chain and Airbel.  Major ResponsibilitiesThe Business Development Senior Officer (ECHO), will be responsible for leading a portfolio of business development opportunities, ensuring that all proposals are compelling and submitted in accordance with IRC and Donor policies.Business Development Process (80%)ECHO oversight: Provide IRC Germany oversight to opportunities submitted under ECHO’s Strategic Policies and Strategic Humanitarian Supply Chain HIPs. This will include completing ECHO pre-award checklists and uploads to APPEL. Proposal leadership: Outside of the ECHO HIP season, will serve as Proposal Lead for funding opportunities assigned by the Head of Business Development.- Lead the overall proposal development process to ensure submissions are compliant, responsive, and compelling. - Support the technical team to position for anticipated calls, including pre-development of concept notes.- Project manage proposals ensuring internal approvals in line with external submission deadlines- Coordinate with country programs and partners to collect the documents and inputs needed for each proposal Proposal Budget development: Serve as Budget Lead for funding opportunities assigned by the Head of Business Development.- Develop proposal budgets to ensure consistency and accuracy across projects. Design, draft, refine, and finalize budgets and budget narratives (as needed) that are reflective of program design costs.- Ensure appropriate internal formats and donor formats for budget development are used.- Coordinate and liaise with country program finance and grants staff on proposals, providing guidance and feedback on workplans, deadlines, and proposal parameters.- Secure approvals across departments for submissions.Process Support and Feedback (10%)BD Process Improvements: Work on departmental and organisational initiatives to improve IRC’s BD processes.- Support refinement of business development processes for Technical Excellence.- Attend key cross-unit and cross-departmental meetings regarding business development to maintain an in-depth understanding of IRC funding streams and business development priorities.ECHO Awards Management and Compliance (10%)Awards Management: Act as IRC Germany’s post-award focal point for Technical Excellence and Global Supply Chain ECHO awards. - Provide ad-hoc compliance guidance to grants team on ECHO awards- Coordinate with grants team to ensure timely submissions of reports on APPEL.- Monitor ECHO portfolio through participation in project implementation meetings, ensuring progress against objectives and compliance with ECHO guidelines.- Manage donor relationship with ECHO across portfolio.Your ProfileEssential- Experience preparing or submitting proposals to ECHO- 5+ years of progressive work experience connected to business development and working in or closely with Technical teams - Highly collaborative and pro-active colleague with a talent for delivering results with cross-functional groups- Advanced Microsoft Office skills (Excel, PowerPoint) and experience with organizational information and financial systems- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in a multi-cultural environment - University degree in Business Administration, Finance, International Development or a relevant field, or equivalent work experience- You have English language skills at C1 and German B1 according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CERF) (https://www.europaeischer-referenzrahmen.de/)  Desired- Experience working with IRC systems is a plus- Dedication to diversity, equity and inclusion, and a strong passion for our mission- Comfortable adapting to new challenges and dynamic priorities, while maintaining professional grace - Fluency in French, Spanish or Arabic language a plus We Offer- Meaningful work within a collaborative team- A starting salary between 60,028 and 67,090 Euro gross per year as well as an annual salary increase- Attractive employee benefits such as gym membership, company pension scheme, shopping vouchers, childcare subsidy, job bike leasing, subsidized Deutschlandticket (national public transport), and access to timely and confidential psychological support if needed- 30 days of annual leave and special leave days- Flexible hybrid-work options (working hours, office/homebased)- Training and professional development opportunities, including access to free language courses- Assistance services for people with disabilities, if required.We look forward to receiving your application (including CV and – if available – three references) via our application portal (https://theirc.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/External_Careers/job/Berlin-Germany/Business-Development-Senior-Officer--d-f-m---ECHO-_JR00005896) – even if you do not meet all the listed requirements. For questions regarding the position, please contact Burrhus Njanjo (HR.Deutschland@rescue.org (https://mailto:HR.Deutschland@rescue.org) ).As an organization committed to an empowering work environment, equal opportunities, and against any form of discrimination, we welcome applications from people regardless of their origin, religion, gender, sexual orientation, disabilities, age, or other characteristics protected by applicable law. We particularly encourage people with personal or family experience of flight and migration to apply.With equal qualifications, we give preference to applications from people with severe disabilities. If you have any questions about accessible applications or inclusion, please feel free to contact our Inclusion Officer, Christine Mader (christine.mader@rescue.org (https://mailto:christine.mader@rescue.org) ).To ensure equal opportunities, we kindly ask you to refrain from including photos in your application documents.Please submit your application by 29th November 2026.All IRC workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct (https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct) . On this basis, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding (https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding) , Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Anti-Retaliation.You can find more information about IRC Germany at IRCDeutschland.org (https://www.irc-deutschland.org/) .Homeoffice:Umfang: Nach Vereinbarung

jobs.description: The German Institute of Human Nutrition Potsdam-Rehbruecke (DIfE) (https://www.dife.de/) is a member of the Leibniz Association. The institute’s mission is to conduct experimental and clinical research in the field of nutrition and health, with the aim of understanding the molecular basis of nutrition-dependent diseases, and of developing new strategies for treatment and prevention.The Department Molecular Physiology of Exercise and Nutrition (MPEN) (https://www.dife.de/forschung/abteilungen-und-forschungsgruppen/molekulare-physiologie-der-bewegung-und-ernaehrung/) is inviting applications for1 Doctoral Student (m/f/d)starting as soon as possible.Project descriptionThis project investigates the regulation and metabolic fate of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) in the liver, with a particular focus on their role in metabolic health and fatty liver disease. Using mouse models, cell culture systems, and state-of-the-art metabolic approaches, we aim to understand the mechanisms governing hepatic SCFA uptake and how these processes are regulated by nutritional states, including fasting and feeding, and altered under pathological conditions such as metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). A central focus of the project is to determine the intracellular fate of SCFAs, investigating when they serve as energy substrates, building blocks for anabolic processes, or regulators of gene expression through epigenetic modifications. By combining in vivo and in vitro experiments with stable isotope tracing and metabolic flux analysis, we aim to uncover how hepatic SCFA metabolism is regulated and how it contributes to liver function and metabolic disease.Specifically, the candidate will:- Plan and perform in vivo metabolic experiments in mice to investigate hepatic SCFA uptake, metabolism, and substrate utilization under different nutritional and disease conditions.- Design and conduct stable isotope tracing experiments, both in vivo and in cultured cells, to characterize SCFA uptake, intracellular metabolic fluxes, and incorporation into downstream metabolites and cellular components.- Establish and perform cell culture experiments, including work with primary hepatocytes, to investigate the molecular mechanisms controlling SCFA metabolism.- Investigate the contribution of SCFAs to energy metabolism, anabolic pathways, and epigenetic modifications, including histone acylation.- Perform downstream molecular and biochemical analyses of tissues and biological samples, including metabolomics, protein analyses, and measurements of metabolic intermediates.- Contribute to the management and maintenance of mouse colonies, including breeding, genotyping, and experimental planning.Requirements and Skills- A master's degree in biochemistry, molecular biology, physiology, nutritional sciences, or a related discipline.- Prior hands-on experience with stable isotope tracing and metabolic flux analysis is a key requirement for this position.- A strong background in intermediary metabolism, particularly hepatic glucose, lipid, or fatty acid metabolism.- Practical experience with cell culture techniques and molecular and biochemical assays.- Experience with mass spectrometry-based metabolomics and the analysis of isotope labeling data is an advantage.- Strong analytical skills, scientific curiosity, and the ability to plan and conduct experiments independently.- Excellent communication skills in English and a collaborative approach to research.We offer:- Intensive scientific support, close collaboration with cooperating institutions and enrolment in a local PhD program- Excellent technical equipment, a wide range of experimental methods and a dynamic and interactive research environment- Remuneration according to TV-L, level 13 (65 %), plus annual special payment and company pension scheme- Family-friendly working conditions (certificate “audit berufundfamilie”)- Supporting of mobility with a jobticket for using the public transport- Easy accessibility by public transport or car (including free parking)- 30 days of vacation- Participation in the benefits program for employees („Corporate Benefits“)The advertised position is available for 3 years.We promote the employment of people with severe disabilities and are committed to equal opportunities for them. Applicants with severe disabilities will be given preferential consideration if they have the same qualifications.We look forward to your application!Please send your documents (cover letter explaining your motivation, CV, copies of degrees/certificates and references) as a single pdf-file before November 25th, 2026 via e-mail to jobs@dife.de.For further information please do not hesitate to contact:Prof. Dr. Maximilian KleinertHead of Department Molecular Physiology of Exercise and NutritionE-Mail: Maximilian.Kleinert@dife.deWe process your application documents for the purpose of carrying out the application procedure in accordance with Art. 6 para. 1 lit. b) GDPR, Art. 88 GDPR. For more information on the collection, processing and use of personal data by the German Institute of Human Nutrition as part of the application process and your rights under data protection law, please contact the Department of Human Resources and Social Services (jobs@dife.de).
